parts.text: 李太白邀君同游。|诗吟蜀道之险峻，歌咏云海之壮丽。|且循一声长吟，从心中歧路，行向万里沧海。
Li Bai invites you to wander. | Hear the perilous road to Shu, and the splendour of a sea of clouds. | Follow the song, from the heart’s uncertain paths towards the open sea.
门外是长安夜色，门内是一席灯火。|这一程，先从繁华深处，听一颗未得舒展的心。
门扉微凉。
隔着一道门，尘世的喧声渐远，眼前的灯影渐近。
灯火深处，且入诗中。
随这一线渐开的光，走入诗人的心境；盛筵之中，也会有难言的孤独。
Beyond the door lies Chang’an at night; within, a banquet glows. | Our journey begins amid splendour, with a heart that cannot find ease.
The door is cool to the touch.
Beyond the threshold, the noise of the world recedes and the lamplight draws us in.
Beyond the lamplight, let us enter the poem.
Follow the widening light into the poet’s state of mind. Even a splendid feast may hold an unspoken loneliness.
清酒映灯，珍馐满席。|主人待客的盛意，都在这一案之间；而诗人的心，似乎另有所系。
金樽清酒，斗十千。
一个“金”字，先写器物的华美；酒价极言其贵，盛情也随之可见。
玉盘珍羞，直万钱。
珍羞，是珍贵的美味。“万钱”与“十千”相映，把筵席的丰盛推到眼前。
珍馐入口，心事难消。
这一口浅尝，是我们入诗的铺垫。满席滋味，终究难解心中郁结。
Clear wine catches the lamplight; fine dishes fill the table. | The feast speaks of a host’s generosity, yet the poet’s thoughts are elsewhere.
Clear wine in golden cups, ten thousand coins a measure.
The golden vessel establishes the feast’s splendour. Its extravagant price magnifies the value of the wine and the generosity of the occasion.
Fine delicacies on jade plates, worth ten thousand more.
These are rare delicacies. The two immense prices echo each other, making the abundance of the banquet almost tangible.
A taste of fine food. | Yet the troubled heart finds no ease.
This brief taste is our imagined prelude to the verse. The table offers every pleasure, yet the heart remains troubled.
灯影未动，心绪已乱。|满席佳肴依旧，先前的从容，却渐渐留不住了。
停杯。
杯在手中，却无心再饮。动作忽然顿住，繁华与愁绪，便隔在了这一停之间。
投箸，不能食。
并非佳肴不美，而是心事难平。箸落案头，无须直说愁苦，愁苦已然可见。
The lamplight is still; the heart is restless. | The feast has not changed, but its guest can no longer feel at ease.
I set down my cup.
The cup is close at hand, but the wish to drink has gone. In this arrested gesture, outward splendour meets inward sorrow.
I cast aside my chopsticks. | I cannot eat.
The food has lost none of its richness. It is the troubled heart that cannot accept it. The fallen chopsticks give sorrow a visible form.
满堂繁华，忽然退成寂静。|心中的不甘，还在寻找一个出口。
拔剑。
胸中的不平，化作这一拔。剑锋虽出，心中仍寻不到可以施展的方向。
四顾。|心茫然。
举目四望，却无所适从。这一刻，有想要有所作为的力量，也有无路可行的迷惘。
The splendour of the hall recedes into silence. | An unyielding spirit is still searching for a way forward.
I draw my sword.
The drawn blade gives shape to an agitated spirit. Yet resolve alone cannot reveal where that strength should be directed.
I look about me. | My heart is lost.
The gaze searches every direction and finds no answer. The desire to act remains strong, but it cannot yet find a path.
夜色四合，天地虽阔，去路未明。|且随这未定的目光，在远近高低之间，听一听心中的回声。
廊下无人。
目光向左，只有层层廊影。四顾，是寻路，也是心中反复的追问。
抬眼，是一庭清月。
天宇如此开阔，人的心却仍有阻隔。高处的光，并没有立刻回答眼前的迷惘。
回首，灯火已远。
万家灯色依然，自己的去向却未可知。眼前虽有繁华，心中还缺一个方向。
俯看，归路仍空。
脚下的路默然延伸。景色换了，未解的心事仍在；这便是我们对“心茫然”的回望。
Night closes in. The world is vast, but the way ahead is unclear. | Follow the searching gaze, near and far, high and low, and hear the heart’s unanswered question.
No one in the corridor.
To the left, corridor follows corridor. This searching gaze turns an outward movement into an inward question.
Looking up, I find a courtyard filled with moonlight.
The sky is open and immense, yet the heart still feels confined. Its light offers no immediate answer to the uncertainty below.
Looking back, the lamplight seems far away.
The city’s lights remain, but one traveller’s destination is unknown. There is splendour to see, and still no certain way to follow.
Looking down, the way home is still empty.
The path extends silently below. The view has changed, but the question remains. This imagined passage dwells on the poem’s bewildered heart.
长河横亘，寒气迎面。|方才席间的心事，在想象中，化成了一条难渡的河。
欲渡黄河。|冰塞川。
“欲渡”，是心有所往；“冰塞”，却将这份愿望拦住。难渡的河，也是理想受阻的心境。
A great river bars the way, and cold meets us head on. | The trouble felt at the banquet now takes shape as a river that cannot be crossed.
I would cross the Yellow River. | Ice blocks its course.
The wish to cross expresses purpose; the blocking ice frustrates it. This imagined river makes an inward obstacle visible.
太行苍茫，风雪无边。|河川之外，又一重高山立在前路。
将登太行。|雪满山。
“将登”，又一次向前；“雪满”，又一重阻隔。冰与雪相接，写尽进退维谷，却未写尽求索之心。
The Taihang Mountains stretch into a boundless storm. | Beyond the river, another barrier rises on the road ahead.
I would climb the Taihang Mountains. | Snow fills their heights.
Again comes the wish to advance; again, a barrier. Ice and snow deepen the sense of frustration, while the desire to seek a way remains.
山路到了分岔处，远近皆是未卜之途。|越想向前，越觉脚下难以抉择。
行路难！|行路难！|多歧路，今安在？
短句接连而来，像欲行又止的脚步。“今安在”，问路在何方，也问人生该向何处。
The mountain path divides. Near or far, every road is uncertain. | The stronger the wish to go forward, the harder it is to choose a way.
Hard is the road! | Hard is the road! | So many paths. Where is my way now?
The brief cries break the rhythm like footsteps starting and stopping. The question asks where the road lies, and where a life may turn.
别却席间心事，迎面已是蜀山。|此刻，且换听《蜀道难》的声音：一声惊叹，便将天地撑开。
噫吁嚱！|危乎高哉！|蜀道之难，难于上青天。
还未细说山川，惊叹已经夺声而出。以登天来比蜀道，夸张的想象，让险峻扑面而来。
We leave the troubled banquet behind, and the mountains of Shu rise before us. | Now listen to The Hard Road to Shu: its opening cry expands the world before our eyes.
Ah! | So perilous, so high! | The road to Shu is harder than climbing the blue heavens.
Before any measured description, astonishment bursts out. Comparing this road with climbing heaven makes its peril immediate and overwhelming.
古道藏在崖壁间，石色苍苍。|脚下的通途并非从来便有，诗人把它的开辟，写进了古老传说。
地崩山摧壮士死。|然后，天梯石栈相钩连。
这是五丁开山的传说，不是实录。诗人借神话写开路之艰；抬眼再看，石栈才沿着崖壁相接。
An ancient path clings to the grey cliff. | This passage did not always exist. The poet imagines its opening through an ancient legend.
Earth split, mountains crumbled, and the brave men died. | Only then did skyward ladders and cliff paths link the way.
This is the legend of the five strongmen, not a historical report. Myth evokes the terrible cost of opening a passage; the cliff paths emerge from that imagined upheaval.
云端是日月，足下是江流。|山的高，水的险，即将在一仰一俯之间相逢。
上有六龙回日之高标。
神话中的日车由六龙驾驭，到了这里，也仿佛要回转。山峰之高，已超出寻常尺度。
下有冲波逆折之回川。
目光从天际落入深谷，回旋的激流与高峰相对。一个“上”，一个“下”，把蜀道的险写满天地。
Above the clouds, the sun; beneath our feet, the river. | Height and danger meet as our gaze turns from the sky towards the depths.
Above, a peak so high that the sun’s six dragons turn their chariot back.
In myth, six dragons draw the sun’s chariot. Even they seem forced to turn here. The mountain’s height exceeds every ordinary measure.
Below, a river turns back upon itself in surging waves.
Our gaze falls from the sky into the gorge. The turning torrent answers the towering peak: above and below, peril fills the landscape.
青泥岭上，来路渐隐。|岩峦层层相叠，仿佛没有一段路，肯直直地通向远方。
青泥何盘盘。|百步九折萦岩峦。
“九折”极写曲折，并非要我们数清弯道。山路缠绕岩峦，行人的步履，也被一次次牵回。
On Qingni Ridge, the path behind us fades. | Rocky folds rise one beyond another; no stretch of road seems willing to run straight towards the distance.
How Qingni twists and winds! | In a hundred paces, nine turns coil around the rocky peaks.
The many turns emphasise the path’s winding course, rather than give an exact count. Each bend draws the traveller back around another fold of rock.
夜空低垂，万籁俱寂。|山势高到何处，且听诗人如何把人的身影，放到星辰之间。
扪参历井，仰胁息。
参、井，是星宿之名。仿佛伸手可触，写山之高；仰头不敢呼吸，又把惊险写进了人的身体。
以手抚膺，坐长叹。
“膺”是胸口，“坐”在这里是徒然。手抚胸前，只能长叹；方才的浩瀚，终于落成一声人的叹息。
The night sky hangs low, and every sound is stilled. | How high are these mountains? Listen as the poet places a human figure among the stars.
Reaching past the stars of Shen and Jing, I look up and hold my breath.
Shen and Jing are constellations. To seem close enough to touch them conveys immense height; the held breath makes that height a bodily fear.
With a hand upon my chest, I can only sigh.
The hand returns to the chest. Here the Chinese word zuo means in vain, not sitting down. Beneath the vast sky, the traveller can only heave a long sigh.
林深处，枝影交错。|天色暗了，山中的声音，反而一声声清晰起来。
但见悲鸟，号古木。
古木深深，鸟声凄切。一个“悲”字，让本来无情的山林，染上行人心中的愁。
雄飞雌从，绕林间。
鸟影成双，来回绕林；行人却置身陌生的山路。声音与身影，使这片幽深更添孤寂。
Deep in the forest, shadows of branches intertwine. | As the light fades, the sounds of the mountains grow strangely clear.
Only sorrowing birds cry among ancient trees.
Ancient trees surround a mournful call. The word sorrowing colours the forest with the traveller’s own unease.
The male flies; the female follows, circling through the woods.
The birds move together among the trees, while the traveller faces an unfamiliar road. Their calls and circling forms deepen the sense of solitude.
一轮寒月，照着无人的山径。|且听，寂静里有什么声音，正从林间传来。
又闻子规，啼夜月。|愁，空山。
子规，便是杜鹃。啼声传过山谷，越有回音，越觉空寂；诗人的愁，也随着这一声，落满空山。
A cold moon lights a deserted mountain path. | Listen. Something is calling through the stillness of the trees.
And the cuckoo calls beneath the moon. | Sorrow fills the empty mountains.
Zigui is a cuckoo. Its call crosses the valley; the echo makes the emptiness more distinct. Through that sound, sorrow seems to fill the mountains.
林声渐远，水气渐浓。|方才的幽静，被深谷里奔来的声浪，层层推开。
飞湍瀑流争喧豗。|砯崖转石，万壑雷。
“争”，写水势奔涌；“雷”，写声响震谷。方才是鸟鸣衬静，此刻是万壑齐响，险境骤然逼近。
The forest sounds recede, and the air grows heavy with spray. | The hush gives way to a rising roar from the ravine.
Rapids and waterfalls roar together. | They strike the cliffs and tumble stones: thunder in ten thousand ravines.
The torrents seem to compete in their rush, and their sound becomes thunder. Birdsong once made the stillness deeper; now the whole ravine resounds with danger.
蜀门在此，万山收束成一线。|行至剑阁，山川的险峻，又添了一重关塞的森严。
剑阁峥嵘而崔嵬。
群峰夹峙，关隘高耸。剑阁之险，先落在这逼仄的地势之间。
一夫当关。
一人守住要隘，便仿佛扼住整条通路。此句着重写的，是关口易守难攻。
万夫，莫开。
一与万，形成极强的对照。关门森然，也让诗意从山川之险，转向对人事的警惕。
Here stands the gateway to Shu, where mountains narrow to a single passage. | At Sword Gate, the peril of the landscape takes on the severity of a guarded frontier.
Sword Gate rises, sheer and towering.
The peaks close in around a towering pass. Its danger begins with the narrowness of the terrain itself.
One man guards the pass.
A single defender seems able to command the whole passage. The line stresses how readily the narrow pass can be held.
Ten thousand cannot break through.
One stands against ten thousand. This striking contrast shifts the poem from the dangers of the landscape towards concern about those who command it.
锦城深处，烟火繁华。|然而一路的惊心尚未散去，眼前的热闹，也留不住那一份牵挂。
锦城虽云乐。|不如，早还家。
锦城，指成都。不是不见它的繁华，而是牵挂胜过留恋；这一声劝归，含着对远行人的关切。
Deep in the Brocade City, daily life flourishes. | Yet the perils of the journey still weigh on the heart; even this bustle cannot silence its concern.
Though the Brocade City is a place of pleasure, | better to return home soon.
The Brocade City is Chengdu. The poem acknowledges its pleasures, yet concern outweighs their appeal. The counsel to return is also an expression of care.
千重山外，还有故园。|《蜀道难》的行吟将尽，诗人的目光，却仍向着远处。
侧身西望。|长咨嗟。
西望之间，惊叹已化作长叹。蜀道的雄奇与忧思，一同留在这未尽的声音里。
Beyond a thousand mountain folds, home remains. | The Hard Road to Shu is drawing to its close, but the poet’s gaze still reaches into the distance.
I turn and gaze westward. | A long, deep sigh.
The westward gaze turns astonishment into a lingering sigh. The grandeur of Shu and the poem’s concern remain together in that unresolved sound.
山声渐息，溪色转青。|让我们回到《行路难》，在迟疑之外，听见另一种可能。
闲来垂钓，碧溪上。
此处用姜尚的典故：相传他在溪边垂钓，后来得到重用。诗人借前人的际遇，为未展的抱负，留住一线希望。
The mountains fall quiet; the stream turns green. | We return to Hard Is the Road, and listen for a possibility beyond hesitation.
At leisure, I fish beside a clear green stream.
This recalls the story of Jiang Shang, who fished before being called to serve. His eventual recognition offers the poet hope that unfulfilled ambition may yet find its hour.
一枕江声，浮生入梦。|清溪的等候未远，诗人的思绪，又随着一叶舟轻轻荡开。
忽复乘舟，梦日边。
又用伊尹的典故：相传他受商汤任用前，曾梦见乘舟经过日旁。两个典故接续，低回的心境，渐渐转向期待。
With river sounds beside the pillow, life drifts into a dream. | The thought of waiting by a stream opens into another image: a boat upon the water.
Then, in a dream, I sail in a boat beside the sun.
Another allusion follows: before being called to serve Tang, Yi Yin was said to have dreamed of sailing beside the sun. These remembered possibilities turn hesitation towards expectation.
长夜将尽，风起沧海。|前路仍然辽阔，心中的声音，却已渐渐有了力量。
长风破浪，会有时。|直挂云帆，济沧海。
“会有时”，并非眼前已无风浪，而是相信终有施展抱负的一天。于是云帆高挂，漫长的求索，有了继续向前的勇气。
The long night is ending; wind rises over the sea. | The way ahead remains vast, but the voice within begins to gather strength.
One day I shall ride the long wind and break the waves. | I shall raise my cloud-high sail and cross the vast blue sea.
One day does not mean the waves have already vanished. It declares faith that ambition will find its moment. The rising sail carries the courage to continue.
山海仍在，行歌未止。|《蜀道难》以长叹寄关切，《行路难》以云帆见信念。|两首诗，各有回声；愿君怀此心，行向自己的远方。

Mountains and seas remain; the song continues. | The Hard Road to Shu closes in a sigh of concern; Hard Is the Road finds faith in a rising sail. | Each poem keeps its own voice. Carry their echoes towards your own horizon.
扪参历井仰胁息，以手抚膺坐长叹。参、井是星宿名；扪是摸，膺是胸，坐在这里是徒然。诗人夸张地写山高近星，又以屏息、抚胸、长叹写行人的惊惧。伸向星空的手回到胸前，让浩瀚山川与人的感受相接。

Reaching past the stars of Shen and Jing, I look up and hold my breath. With a hand upon my chest, I can only sigh. Shen and Jing are constellations. Seeming to touch them is an exaggeration of height; the held breath, hand on the chest and long sigh convey the traveller’s fear. Here zuo means in vain, not sitting down.

Ah! How perilous, how high!
The road to Shu is harder than climbing to the blue sky.
Cancong and Yufu—how distant the founding of their kingdom!
For forty-eight thousand years it had no passage to the lands of Qin.
Westward, on Mount Taibai, only a bird’s path
could cross towards the heights of Mount Emei.
The earth split, mountains crumbled, and the strong men died;
only then were skyward stairs and cliff paths joined.
Above stand peaks that turn back the sun’s six-dragon chariot;
below, wild currents twist and surge.
Even the yellow crane cannot fly across;
apes and monkeys grieve at the climb.
How the Qingni road coils!
A hundred steps, nine turns around the cliffs.
Touching the stars of Shen and Jing, I look up with breath held;
hand upon my chest, I can only sigh.

Sword Gate towers, sheer and formidable.
One man guards the pass; ten thousand cannot break through.
If the keeper is not loyal, he turns into a wolf or jackal.
At dawn beware of fierce tigers; at dusk beware of long snakes.
They bare their teeth and suck blood, killing people like cutting hemp.
Though the Brocade City offers pleasure, better to return home soon.
The road to Shu is harder than climbing to the blue sky;
turning west, I sigh at length.
